## Main result

I fit a nonstationary generalized extreme value (GEV) model to annual maximum daily rainfall at Houston Hobby Airport. The location parameter changes linearly with year, while the scale and shape parameters are constant.

The estimated 2026 return levels are:

- **10-year rainfall:** 195 mm, with a 95% credible interval of 168 to 237 mm.
- **100-year rainfall:** 352 mm, with a 95% credible interval of 261 to 584 mm.

The fitted trend is small and uncertain. The model estimates that both return levels increased by 4 mm from 1986 to 2026, with a 95% interval from -7 to 16 mm. Therefore, this record does **not** provide clear evidence of an increase.

## Data preparation

```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| output: false
using Pkg
here = dirname(@__FILE__)
Pkg.activate(here)
Pkg.instantiate()

using CEVE543Utils
using CairoMakie, CSV, DataFrames, Dates, Distributions, LaTeXStrings
using Printf, Random, Statistics
using FlexiChains: summarystats

rng = MersenneTwister(543)
set_theme!(theme_minimal(); fontsize=14)
colors = Makie.wong_colors()
```

The daily record begins in 1930, but some years contain too many missing observations. I kept a year only when it had at least 350 valid daily readings and excluded 2026 because it is incomplete. This assumes that missing days are unrelated to the amount of rainfall.

```{julia}
#| label: prepare-data
#| output: false
daily_all = CSV.read(joinpath(here, "hobby-daily.csv"), DataFrame)
daily_all.year = year.(daily_all.date)

days_per_year = combine(groupby(daily_all, :year), nrow => :n_days)
keep = days_per_year.year[(days_per_year.n_days .>= 350) .& (days_per_year.year .<= 2025)]
daily = filter(r -> r.year in keep, daily_all)

covariates = CSV.read(joinpath(here, "covariates.csv"), DataFrame)
annmax = combine(groupby(daily, :year), :prcp_mm => maximum => :y)
annmax = sort(innerjoin(annmax, covariates; on=:year), :year)
annmax.year_centered = annmax.year .- 2006
```

This rule retains **80 annual maxima**, from 1940 through 2025. The highest annual maximum is 306.6 mm in 2017.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-data
#| fig-cap: "Annual maximum daily rainfall in the retained years."
fig = Figure(; size=(700, 330))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="year", ylabel="annual maximum rainfall (mm)")
scatter!(ax, annmax.year, annmax.y; color=colors[1], markersize=7)
fig
```

## Model choice

I used annual maxima and a GEV rather than peaks over threshold because it gives one approximately independent observation per year and requires fewer choices about thresholds and storm declustering. The tradeoff is that it uses less information than a peaks-over-threshold model.

For year $t$, the model is

$$
Y_t \sim \operatorname{GEV}(\mu_t,\sigma,\xi),
\qquad
\mu_t = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1(t-2006).
$$

I allowed only the location to trend. With 80 annual maxima, adding trends to the scale or shape would be difficult to estimate and would make the 2066 extrapolation less stable. I used the Bayesian fit in `CEVE543Utils`, its default priors on the intercept, scale, and shape, and a weakly regularizing $N(0,10)$ prior for the standardized location slope.

```{julia}
#| label: fit-models
#| output: false
trend_fit = gevfitbayes(
    annmax,
    :y;
    locationcovid=[:year_centered],
    trend_priors=(location=Normal(0, 10),),
    rng=rng,
    progress=false,
)

stationary_fit = gevfitbayes(
    annmax,
    :y;
    rng=MersenneTwister(543),
    progress=false,
)
```

The chains mixed well. All trend-model $\widehat R$ values are below 1.01, and all bulk effective sample sizes exceed 1,700.

```{julia}
#| label: diagnostics
diagnostics = DataFrame(summarystats(trend_fit.estimate))
select(diagnostics, :param, :ess_bulk, :rhat)
```

## Return levels and change

```{julia}
#| label: calculate-results
#| output: false
interval(v) = quantile(v, [0.025, 0.5, 0.975])

report_years = [1986, 2026, 2066]
x_report = report_years .- 2006
rl10 = returnlevel(trend_fit, 10; locationcov=[x_report])
rl100 = returnlevel(trend_fit, 100; locationcov=[x_report])

coefs = params(trend_fit)
location_slope = coefs.β_location[:, 2]
```

| Quantity | Posterior median | 95% credible interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2026 10-year rainfall | 195 mm | 168 to 237 mm |
| 2026 100-year rainfall | 352 mm | 261 to 584 mm |
| Change, 1986 to 2026 | +4 mm | -7 to +16 mm |
| Change, 2026 to 2066 | +4 mm | -7 to +16 mm |

Because only the GEV location changes, the modeled absolute change is the same for the 10- and 100-year return levels. The location trend is 0.11 mm per year, with a 95% interval from -0.17 to 0.39 mm per year.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-return-levels
#| fig-cap: "Posterior medians and 95% credible intervals for the 10- and 100-year return levels. Values after 2025 are projections."
plot_years = collect(minimum(annmax.year):2066)
x_plot = plot_years .- 2006

function column_summary(x)
    lower = [quantile(c, 0.025) for c in eachcol(x)]
    center = [median(c) for c in eachcol(x)]
    upper = [quantile(c, 0.975) for c in eachcol(x)]
    (; lower, center, upper)
end

rl10_plot = column_summary(returnlevel(trend_fit, 10; locationcov=[x_plot]))
rl100_plot = column_summary(returnlevel(trend_fit, 100; locationcov=[x_plot]))

fig = Figure(; size=(760, 420))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="year", ylabel="daily rainfall (mm)")
vspan!(ax, 2025, 2066; color=(:gray, 0.10))

for (summary, color, label) in (
    (rl10_plot, colors[2], "10-year level"),
    (rl100_plot, colors[1], "100-year level"),
)
    band!(ax, plot_years, summary.lower, summary.upper; color=(color, 0.18))
    lines!(ax, plot_years, summary.center; color=color, linewidth=3, label=label)
end

scatter!(ax, annmax.year, annmax.y; color=:black, markersize=5, label="annual maxima")
vlines!(ax, [2025]; color=:gray45, linestyle=:dash)
axislegend(ax; position=:lt)
save(joinpath(here, "return-level-trend.png"), fig; px_per_unit=2)
fig
```

The posterior interval for the slope includes zero, and a stationary GEV gives nearly the same 2026 return levels: 191 mm for 10 years and 353 mm for 100 years. I therefore interpret the trend estimate as weak evidence rather than a detected increase.

The published estimate summarized in the lab prompt is an increase of 1.93 mm per year, with a 95% interval from 1.50 to 2.35 mm per year [@fagnant_spatiotemporal:2020]. My estimate is much smaller. Differences in record-screening rules and model structure can contribute to the disagreement.

## Projection and limitations

The 2066 projection assumes that the same linear location trend continues for another 40 years while the scale and shape remain constant. Under that assumption, the median change from 2026 to 2066 is another 4 mm. However, the interval from -7 to 16 mm includes both a decrease and an increase, so the direction of future change is uncertain.

The Bayesian intervals include parameter uncertainty within this model. They do not include uncertainty about the missing-data rule, the choice of GEV instead of GPD, the linear functional form, possible changes in measurement, or whether the future climate follows the historical relationship. Those omissions are especially important for the 100-year level and for extrapolation to 2066.

## Answers to the four questions

1. In 2026, the estimated 10-year rainfall is **195 mm** and the estimated 100-year rainfall is **352 mm**.
2. Their 95% credible intervals are **168 to 237 mm** and **261 to 584 mm**, respectively.
3. From 1986 to 2026, the estimated increase is **4 mm**, with a 95% interval of **-7 to 16 mm**. The data do not show a clear increase.
4. From 2026 to 2066, the model projects another **4 mm** change, again with a 95% interval of **-7 to 16 mm**, assuming the linear location trend continues and the scale and shape remain constant.
